title: Inverse Galois Problem: D₄ Realization via X⁴−2
description: Proves |Gal(X⁴−2/ℚ)| = 8, realizing the dihedral group D₄ as a Galois group over ℚ. Lower bound: 4 | |Gal| from degree of X⁴−2. Upper bound: X²+1 has no root in AdjoinRoot(X⁴−2) via ℝ-embedding argument, forcing [SF:ℚ] = 8. Also proves cyclic group realization via cyclotomic fields. 27 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

mathlibDependencies.description: Splitting field for Galois group computation

overview.historicalContext:
The **Inverse Galois Problem** — which groups arise as Galois groups over ℚ — has been open since Hilbert's era. The abelian case is solved by the **Kronecker-Weber theorem** (every abelian extension of ℚ is cyclotomic), and symmetric groups $S_n$ are realizable for all $n$ (by Hilbert's irreducibility theorem). Non-abelian realizations require explicit constructions.

$D_4$ (the dihedral group of order 8) is perhaps the simplest non-abelian example. Its realization as $\text{Gal}(X^4-2/\mathbb{Q})$ is classical: the splitting field $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt[4]{2}, i)$ has degree 8 over $\mathbb{Q}$, and the Galois group acts by $\sigma: \sqrt[4]{2} \mapsto i\sqrt[4]{2}$ (rotation of order 4) and $\tau: i \mapsto -i$ (complex conjugation, reflection of order 2).

The key lemma — $i \notin \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt[4]{2})$ — follows immediately from $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt[4]{2}) \subset \mathbb{R}$, giving a clean **ℝ-embedding argument** that avoids explicit degree calculations. This approach is formalized here as `embedAdjoinRootX4Sub2InReal` via `AdjoinRoot.lift`.
overview.problemStatement: Prove |Gal(X⁴−2/ℚ)| = 8, identifying the Galois group as D₄.
overview.proofStrategy: Lower bound: X⁴−2 irreducible (Eisenstein p=2), so 4 | [SF:ℚ] → 4 | |Gal|. Upper bound via ℝ-embedding: AdjoinRoot(X⁴−2) embeds into ℝ (via the real fourth root ⁴√2). Since X²+1 has no real root, it has no root in this adjoin, so [SF:AdjoinRoot] = 2 (need to adjoin i). Total: [SF:ℚ] = 4 × 2 = 8.
keyInsights: **ℝ-embedding trick**: ℚ(⁴√2) ⊂ ℝ (via ⁴√2 ∈ ℝ). X²+1 has no real root (x²+1 ≥ 1 > 0). Hence X²+1 has no root in ℚ(⁴√2), so [ℚ(⁴√2, i):ℚ(⁴√2)] = 2.
**D₄ structure**: D₄ is generated by rotation r (order 4: ⁴√2 → i·⁴√2) and reflection s (order 2: i → -i). The 8 elements are {1, r, r², r³, s, sr, sr², sr³}.
**Cyclic realization**: For prime p, |Gal(Φ_p/ℚ)| = p−1 (cyclic of order p−1). This gives cyclic Galois groups for every prime minus 1.
**General degree divisibility**: For monic irreducible f of degree d, d | [SF:ℚ] — a useful general lemma.

**Three-constraint squeeze**: 4 | n and n | 8 gives n ∈ {4, 8}; n ≠ 4 (by ℝ-embedding) pins n = 8. The `interval_cases` tactic materializes this by generating goals for n ∈ {4,5,6,7,8} and dispatching each — a pattern applicable to any finite cardinality determination.

sections.title: Part I: General Degree Divisibility Lemma
sections.summary: irred_monic_degree_dvd_splitting_finrank: for monic irreducible f of degree d, d | [SF(f):ℚ]. Proved via tower law with adjoin of a root; generalizes Mathlib's prime-only version.
sections.mathContext: For $F \subseteq K \subseteq L$: $[L:F] = [L:K]\cdot[K:F]$. With $K=\mathbb{Q}(\alpha)$ ($\alpha$ root of $f$), $[K:F]=\deg(f)$, giving $\deg(f) \mid [\text{SF}:F]$.

sections.title: Part II: Cyclic Galois Groups via Cyclotomic Fields
sections.summary: cyclotomic_prime_gal_card: |Gal(Φ_p/ℚ)| = p-1. cyclotomic_prime_gal_isCyclic. cyclic_galois_realization: cyclic group of order p-1 is realizable over ℚ for every prime p.
sections.mathContext: $\text{Gal}(\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_p)/\mathbb{Q}) \cong (\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^\times$, cyclic of order $p-1$ (since $\mathbb{F}_p^\times$ is cyclic). Realizes $C_n$ for all $n = p-1$, $p$ prime.

sections.title: Part III: X⁴−2 Properties and Fourth Root Lemmas
sections.summary: Irreducibility (Eisenstein p=2), lower bound 4 | |Gal|, fourth_root_of_unity_primitive, and the key theorem: the splitting field of X⁴-2 contains a root of X²+1.
sections.mathContext: $X^4-2$ irreducible over $\mathbb{Q}$ (Eisenstein, $p=2$). $4 \mid |\text{Gal}|$. Fourth root of unity: if $c^4=1$, $c\neq\pm 1$, then $c^2+1=0$. Among the 4 roots of $X^4-2$, some pair $a,b$ satisfies $(a/b)^2+1=0$.

sections.title: Part IV: ℝ-Embedding Rules Out |Gal| = 4
sections.summary: fourthRootOfTwo in ℝ. embedAdjoinRootX4Sub2InReal via AdjoinRoot.lift. x_sq_add_1_no_root_in_adjoin_root_x4_sub_2. x4_sub_2_gal_card_ne_four: rank-nullity + no-root contradiction eliminates |Gal|=4.
sections.mathContext: $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt[4]{2}) \hookrightarrow \mathbb{R}$; $X^2+1$ has no real root (since $x^2+1 \geq 1 > 0$). If $|\text{Gal}|=4$, then $\text{SF} \cong \text{AdjoinRoot}(X^4-2) \subset \mathbb{R}$, but $\text{SF}$ contains a root of $X^2+1$ — contradiction.

sections.title: Part V: Upper Bound and Main Theorem |Gal| = 8
sections.summary: roots_in_adjoin: all roots of X⁴-2 lie in ℚ(α,ω). x4_sub_2_gal_card_dvd_8: |Gal| | 8 via tower law. x4_sub_2_gal_card: three-constraint squeeze pins |Gal|=8. d4_realizable: D₄ realization existential.
sections.mathContext: All roots $r$ of $X^4-2$ satisfy $r/\alpha \in \{1,-1,\omega,-\omega\}$, so $\text{SF} = \mathbb{Q}(\alpha,\omega)$. Tower: $[\mathbb{Q}(\alpha,\omega):\mathbb{Q}] \leq 2\cdot4=8$. With $4 \mid n$, $n\mid 8$, $n\neq4$: $n=8$.

conclusion.summary: D₄ Galois realization proved: 27 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms. |Gal(X⁴−2/ℚ)| = 8 established via degree lower bound and ℝ-embedding upper bound.
conclusion.implications: This adds D₄ to the gallery's Galois group realizations (alongside S₃, F₂₀). The ℝ-embedding argument is a clean non-algebraic proof that i ∉ ℚ(⁴√2), avoiding explicit degree calculations.
openQuestions: Can the full structure of D₄ as a semidirect product ℤ/4ℤ ⋊ ℤ/2ℤ be identified in the Galois action?
Can the Galois group of X^n - p be computed for all n, p in Lean?
Is there a general criterion for when Gal(X^n - a/ℚ) is dihedral?
